audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradict the page's own why-text: row 0 reads Skill while whys[0] says K'Sante all-ins you at level 1; row 4 reads Skill while whys[4] says Hemoplague 'gives you the kill'; rows 5 and 6 read K'Sante while whys[5] says roughly even and whys[6] says you win the extended trades.
audit.why: The packet chart is K'Sante/K'Sante/K'Sante/Skill/Vladimir/Skill/Vladimir — an exact match for the seven why-rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 4, 5 and 6 flipped as four matched full/content pairs in one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out is named on eleven strings and its cooldown never given; the level-6 spike described the squishy window without saying how long it lasts or how often it comes back.
audit.why: All Out is 120/100/80s — the same 120s as Hemoplague at rank 1, so at 6 the two ultimates trade one-for-one and by rank 3 his comes back first.
audit.corrected: 120s/80s written into spikes[1].text, dosFull[0].d and the cooldown block, alongside Path Maker's 14s and Ntofo Strikes' 3.5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanical errors. The page says Ntofo Strikes gives a 'third-hit knock-up' and tells you to pool it — Riot's text says the shockwave fires at 2 stacks and pulls enemies in. And nothing anywhere mentions that Path Maker stops knocking back and stunning while he is All Out.
audit.why: The pull-versus-knock-up error changes what you do about it, and the mirror already corrected the same phrasing on K'Sante's side, so leaving it here would put the two pages in conflict. The All Out stun loss is the single best reason to fight him during his ultimate rather than before it. Path Maker also deals true damage, so stacking MR does not read that trade correctly.
audit.corrected: Pull replaces knock-up in spikes[0].text and early; the All Out stun loss written into spikes[1].text and dosFull[0].d; true damage noted in the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appeared only as a generic template line in report[8].t with no ability named and no timing.
audit.why: The healing is All Out itself — it is a level-6 problem, not a laning-phase one, so the buy is timed to his ultimate rather than to a wave.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds tied to the All Out window in spikes[1].text and to the ultimate in the cooldown block.

edits.before: - K'Sante All Out: matchup-defining — His duelist mode. Poke when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - K'Sante All Out: 120s at rank 1, 80s maxed — it heals him, so buy Grievous Wounds. - Path Maker: 14s stun, and it deals true damage. - Ntofo Strikes: 3.5s, pulls on the second stack. - Pool: 28s.

edits.before: His duelist mode. Poke when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 120s at rank 1 — while he is All Out his Path Maker no longer stuns you.

edits.before: K'Sante's early spike is his, not yours: with two points he chunks you on Ntofo Strikes stacks and can W-charge a stun through your minions. Don't try to trade back into a full E stack — pool the third-hit knock-up rather than eat the stun, and just farm with Q on cooldown.
edits.after: K'Sante's early spike is his, not yours: Ntofo Strikes is a 3.5s cooldown and its second stack fires a shockwave that pulls you in — not a knock-up. Path Maker charges a stun through minions on 14s, so step out of the 450-range line and farm with Transfusion instead of trading back.

edits.before: Hemoplague swings this. K'Sante All Out re-forms him but strips his tank stats, so your R amplifies the exact window he becomes squishy; drop Hemoplague as he ults in and the burst detonates on a low-resistance target. This is your first real kill threat.
edits.after: Hemoplague swings this. All Out is 120s at rank 1 and trades his defenses for damage, and while he is in it Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns — so bait the ult, drop Hemoplague on the low-resistance form, and note his healing rises: Grievous Wounds first.

edits.before: K'Sante out-trades you at 1-3: Ntofo Strikes stacks a knock-up on the third hit and his W can charge a stun through minions, so an early all-in favours him. Don't contest — last-hit with Transfusion, keep Sanguine Pool for the stun, and give ground rather than eat a full combo.
edits.after: K'Sante out-trades you at 1-3: two Ntofo Strikes stacks fire a shockwave that pulls you in, and Path Maker charges a knockback stun through minions on a 14s cooldown. Don't contest — last-hit with Transfusion, keep Sanguine Pool's 28s for the stun, and give ground rather than eat the combo.

edits.before: Land the W wall-stun to lock you for a full combo before you pool
edits.after: Land Path Maker's stun to lock you for a full combo before you pool

notes: The mirror summary handed to me lists a chart (Skill / Vladimir / Skill / Skill / K'Sante / Vladimir / Vladimir) that matches neither this packet nor its own stated reasoning; I went with the packet chart, which agrees row-for-row with this page's seven why-strings. Worth checking whether that mirror summary was recorded from the wrong matchup before mirror-fix runs. Dauntless Instinct is an ability-into-attack damage mark rather than a conventional auto reset; I did not write it up as a burst tell because the packet's autoreset flag on a passive is the kind of derived-flag misfire the brief warns about, and Riot's text does not describe an attack reset.
